ev.q: The adult immunization schedule is published annually to consolidate and summarize updates to ACIP recommendations on vaccination of adults

public_health_question.v: What changes does the 2023 ACIP immunization schedule make to recommended vaccinations for US adults aged 19 years or older?

ev.q: including several changes to the cover page, tables, notes, and appendix from the 2022 immunization schedule
COVID-19 vaccines have been added to the Tables and to the Notes sections summarizing ACIP recommendations.
Vaccine-specific changes in the 2023 immunization schedule for adults aged ≥19 years include new or updated ACIP recommendations for influenza vaccines
The section has been substantially updated to reflect ACIP’s new recommendations for the use of PCV15 and PCV20
HepB vaccination continues to be universally recommended for all adults aged 19–59 years.
to account for the possibility of an accelerated Twinrix series requiring 4 doses.
the recommendation for additional doses of MMR vaccine (including the third dose of MMR vaccine) in the context of a mumps outbreak setting
In the “Special situations” section for meningococcal serogroup B vaccine, guidance was added
A new section was added summarizing poliovirus vaccination recommendations for adults.
serologic evidence of prior varicella is not necessary for zoster vaccination
The language now states, “pregnancy: HPV vaccination not recommended.”
the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices* (ACIP) approved the Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule for Ages 19 Years or Older, United States, 2023.
Recommended Immunization Schedule for Adults Aged 19 Years or Older — United States, 2023

equity.level_reason: A recommendation schedule with no data; age bounds only define the population of adults aged 19 years or older.

ev.q: Recommended Immunization Schedule for Adults Aged 19 Years or Older — United States, 2023

notes: Annual ACIP adult schedule update listing changes from the 2022 schedule; no quantities are reported. Age thresholds (e.g., ≥60 years for HepB) are recommendation criteria, not comparisons.
